New services must use **`gateway-api`**. The file that decides it is `policy/ingress-class/v3.yaml` on branch `git-access-ab/r3000` of [dshnayder-org/infra](https://github.com/dshnayder-org/infra/blob/git-access-ab/r3000/policy/ingress-class/v3.yaml).

## The mandate

`policy/ingress-class/v3.yaml`, verbatim:

```
# policy: ingress-class
# version: v3   effective: 2026-04-19   status: current
# subject: which ingress implementation new services must use
apiVersion: policy.meridian.io/v1
kind: FleetPolicy
metadata:
  name: ingress-class-v3
spec:
  effectiveFrom: 2026-04-19
  status: current
  setting: gateway-api
```

## Why this one is authoritative

Three versions of the same policy exist and only v3 is live — each file carries its own `status`:

| File | `setting` | `status` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `policy/ingress-class/v1.yaml` | `nginx` | `superseded` (effective `2024-03-11`) |
| `policy/ingress-class/v2.yaml` | `gce-ingress` | `superseded` (effective `2025-06-02`) |
| `policy/ingress-class/v3.yaml` | `gateway-api` | `current` (effective `2026-04-19`) |

v1 says `setting: nginx` and v2 says `setting: gce-ingress`, but both declare `status: superseded` in-file and both are dated earlier, so neither is in force. Every other policy family in the repo (`psa-mode`, `node-image`, `backup-schedule`, `key-rotation`, `log-retention`) follows the identical v1/v2/v3 shape with only v3 marked `current`, so this is the repo's convention, not a one-off. `policy/base.yaml` sets only `kind: FleetPolicyBase` / `spec.inherit: true` and picks no ingress value.

## Nothing else in the branch speaks to it

I enumerated all `3001` tracked paths and grepped the tree case-insensitively for `ingress`, `gateway-api`, `nginx`, `gce-ingress`, `envoy`, `IngressClass`, `ingressClassName`, `Gatekeeper`, `Kyverno`, `ConstraintTemplate` and `ADR`.

- The **only** matches for `ingress` anywhere are the three files above.
- There are **no** ADRs, no networking/standards docs, and no OPA/Gatekeeper/Kyverno constraints — so nothing admission-enforces the choice; `policy/ingress-class/v3.yaml` is a declaration, not a gate.
- There are **no** Ingress or Gateway manifests and no Helm values: the `services/` tree (`identity`, `payments`) contains only `deployment.yaml`, `service.yaml` and `hpa.yaml`. So no manifest contradicts the policy — but none conforms to it either.

Read as one shallow checkout of `git-access-ab/r3000`. Note that a separate change on another branch ([PR #151](https://github.com/dshnayder-org/infra/pull/151)) proposes flipping this same `setting` to `envoy-gateway`; that is not merged into this branch, where the value is `gateway-api`.

## Answer

The reason **is** recorded — but only in a commit message, not anywhere in the repository's files. Commit [`d10fd3d0`](https://github.com/dshnayder-org/infra/commit/d10fd3d016c6af4c0ccbe5ab145257f0f960686c) (`2026-02-01`, *Meridian Platform*) reads verbatim:

```
fix(clusters): pin maxSurge to 0

maxSurge above zero double-books the reserved TPU quota during an upgrade and the whole pool fails to come back; see INC-2219.
```

That commit changed `maxSurge: PLACEHOLDER` → `maxSurge: 0` in the file below, and is the only change to it besides its creation (`cd4d4f6b`).

## The configured value

[`clusters/prod-us-central1/nodepool-batch.yaml`](https://github.com/dshnayder-org/infra/blob/git-access-ab/r3000/clusters/prod-us-central1/nodepool-batch.yaml) — the complete file, all 5 lines:

```yaml
# nodepool-batch
apiVersion: meridian.io/v1
kind: Setting
spec:
  maxSurge: 0
```

`maxSurge: 0` at line `5`. It is the **only** `maxSurge: 0` in the whole repo on `git-access-ab/r3000`; every other node pool I saw uses `1`, `2` or `3`, including the sibling pools in the same directory (`nodepool-general.yaml` and `nodepool-gpu.yaml`, both `maxSurge: 1`) and the batch pool of the neighbouring cluster `clusters/prod-us-central1-2/nodepool-batch.yaml` (`maxSurge: 1`).

## No in-repo documentation

Nothing in the tracked tree explains it. Searching all `3001` tracked paths on this branch: `INC-2219` — `0` matches; `TPU` — `0` matches; `surge` (lowercase) — `0` matches. `clusters/prod-us-central1/README.md` is four lines of ownership only (billing team, `#billing-oncall`), there are no ADRs, and the only docs are `docs/generated/fleet-inventory.txt` and one runbook, neither mentioning surge. So the justification lives solely in git history — if you rely on the file, the rationale is invisible.

## Two things worth flagging

- **This file is shaped unlike a node pool.** Its siblings are `apiVersion: container.meridian.io/v1` / `kind: NodePool` with `metadata.name`, `spec.cluster`, `machineType`, `minNodes`, `maxNodes`. This one is `apiVersion: meridian.io/v1` / `kind: Setting` with a bare `spec.maxSurge` and no `metadata` — yet `kustomization.yaml` lists it as a resource alongside the real pools. Worth confirming it is actually applied as intended.
- **Read on one commit of one branch:** `dshnayder-org/infra` @ `git-access-ab/r3000`, head `d8093b1b`.

## The rationale is recorded, but only in a commit message — no file in the repo explains it

The value lives in [`policy/quota/payments.yaml`](https://github.com/dshnayder-org/infra/blob/git-access-ab/r3000/policy/quota/payments.yaml) (the whole file, 5 lines):

```yaml
# payments
apiVersion: meridian.io/v1
kind: Setting
spec:
  requests.cpu: 480
```

The stated reason is in the commit that set it, [`7095401c`](https://github.com/dshnayder-org/infra/commit/7095401c37840adeadff3e026c889431ad1e2f4d) (`2026-02-02`, `Meridian Platform <platform@meridian.invalid>`), verbatim:

> `fix(policy): pin requests.cpu to 480`
>
> `raised from 320 for the Black Friday freeze and deliberately never lowered, because the rollback would need a control plane resize; see INC-2404.`

So: `480` is not a sizing calculation — it is a peak-season headroom bump from `320` that was intentionally left in place, because reverting it would require a control plane resize.

## Caveats worth knowing

- **`INC-2404` is not in this repo.** No file matches `INC-`, `2404` (outside unrelated `docs/generated/fleet-inventory.txt` cluster ids), `Black`, `freeze`, or `320`. A GitHub issue/PR search for `INC-2404` in `dshnayder-org/infra` returns `0`. The actual capacity analysis is presumably in that incident record, elsewhere.
- **No file-level rationale exists.** There is no ADR, `docs/` note, comment, or PR body covering this value. The repo's only docs are `docs/generated/fleet-inventory.txt` and one Russian-language cluster-recovery runbook.
- **This is not a Kubernetes `ResourceQuota`.** It is a custom `meridian.io/v1 Setting`; grep for `ResourceQuota` across the branch returns `0` matches.
- **Its history is only two commits.** [`cd747ff7`](https://github.com/dshnayder-org/infra/commit/cd747ff7) created the file with `requests.cpu: PLACEHOLDER`, then `7095401c` replaced that placeholder with `480`. The `320` in the message is therefore a prior value from outside this file's git history — it never appears in the tracked content.

## What I checked

- Enumerated **all `3001`** tracked paths on that branch (full pagination, no truncation). No path contains `atlantis`.
- Case-insensitive content search for `atlantis` across all tracked files: `0` matches. A regex search for `atl[a-z]*` also returned `0`. (Control search for `meridian` returns matches, so the search path is working.)
- The `clusters/` tree holds **`468`** cluster directories, all named `<env>-<region>[-N]` with env in `dev`, `staging`, `prod` and region in `us-central1`, `us-east4`, `europe-west1`, `asia-southeast1` — no name-based clusters at all.
- `docs/generated/fleet-inventory.txt` (`9000` lines) lists only `meridian-NNNNN` clusters; `0` lines mention atlantis or any `prod-` name.
- `policy/base.yaml` carries no per-cluster channel defaults (it is only `inherit: true`), so there is no fleet-level fallback that would apply to an undeclared cluster.

## Note on shape

Release channel in this repo lives in one place per cluster — line `10` of `clusters/<name>/cluster.yaml`, e.g. `clusters/prod-us-central1/cluster.yaml:10` → `  releaseChannel: RAPID`. No overlays, kustomize patches, or Terraform variables override it anywhere on this branch, so if `prod-atlantis` existed the answer would be in `clusters/prod-atlantis/cluster.yaml`. That directory does not exist.

If `prod-atlantis` is real, it is defined on a different branch or in a different repo — say which and I will re-check.

## Source

- File: [`docs/generated/fleet-inventory.txt`](https://github.com/dshnayder-org/infra/blob/git-access-ab/r3000/docs/generated/fleet-inventory.txt) on branch `git-access-ab/r3000` (`742500` bytes).
- It is the only generated inventory artifact in the repo — `docs/generated/` contains just this file, and nothing else on the branch produces an inventory output.

## How the numbers were derived

- Count: the file is `9000` lines, every one a cluster record matching `NNNNNN cluster=… region=… nodes=… version=…`. No header, no blank lines, no duplicate cluster names, trailing newline present. There is no self-declared count line in the file, so `9000` is the record count.
- Ordering: unambiguous — the leading index column runs contiguously from `000000` to `008999` in ascending order, so "last" is both the last line and the highest index.

## One caveat

The generated inventory does not describe the `clusters/` source tree on the same branch: it names clusters `meridian-NNNNN`, while the tracked directories are `dev-<region>-N`-style and number in the hundreds, not thousands. The `9000` figure is what the generated artifact says; it is not corroborated by the declarative manifests in the repo.

## Answer

`clusters/prod-us-central1/policy-base.yaml` on `dshnayder-org/infra` branch `git-access-ab/r3000` **is a symlink**. Its blob contains exactly, with no trailing newline:

```
../../policy/base.yaml
```

Relative to its own directory `clusters/prod-us-central1/`, that resolves to **`policy/base.yaml`** at the repo root — a real file (mode `100644`, blob `3f1ad568`, `78` bytes) containing verbatim:

```
apiVersion: policy.meridian.io/v1
kind: FleetPolicyBase
spec:
  inherit: true
```

## Evidence

- Git tree entry for the directory `clusters/prod-us-central1` shows mode `120000` (symlink) for `policy-base.yaml`, blob `11eb2b917b754456c3005c9524cff86e963a59c7`, size `22`: [tree API](https://api.github.com/repos/dshnayder-org/infra/git/trees/git-access-ab/r3000:clusters/prod-us-central1).
- That blob decoded is the 22-byte link target quoted above: [blob 11eb2b91](https://api.github.com/repos/dshnayder-org/infra/git/blobs/11eb2b917b754456c3005c9524cff86e963a59c7).
- Target file: [`policy/base.yaml`](https://github.com/dshnayder-org/infra/blob/git-access-ab/r3000/policy/base.yaml). Symlink path: [`clusters/prod-us-central1/policy-base.yaml`](https://github.com/dshnayder-org/infra/blob/git-access-ab/r3000/clusters/prod-us-central1/policy-base.yaml).

## Caveat worth knowing

The Contents API **hides the symlink** when you ask for the single path: `contents/clusters/prod-us-central1/policy-base.yaml` returns `"type": "file"`, `"size": 78` and the *target's* bytes, so it reads like a regular 78-byte policy file. Only the tree entry (`mode 120000`, `size 22`) and the raw blob reveal the link. The directory listing form of the same API leaks the truth too — it reports `size: 22` for that entry.

Also note `clusters/prod-us-central1/kustomization.yaml` lists only `cluster.yaml`, `nodepool-general.yaml`, `nodepool-batch.yaml`, `nodepool-gpu.yaml` — it does **not** reference `policy-base.yaml`, so nothing in that kustomization consumes the symlink.

Yes — `scripts/rotate-keys.sh` is executable per git's recorded mode on branch `git-access-ab/r3000` of [dshnayder-org/infra](https://github.com/dshnayder-org/infra/blob/git-access-ab/r3000/scripts/rotate-keys.sh). The exact mode is **`100755`**.

## Evidence

This pod has no checkout of that repo, so the mode came from the git object store directly (the read-only equivalent of `git ls-tree`), against branch tip `d8093b1becb8aa5f0ec9b0d9424d96c826676f08`:

`GET repos/dshnayder-org/infra/git/trees/d8093b1becb8aa5f0ec9b0d9424d96c826676f08?recursive=1` →

```
100755	blob	scripts/rotate-keys.sh	f9829bbba1abbf48558fd4cc88931916132a64c7
```

The same entry in the `scripts` subtree (`65bf9eb147096137d44d0cd7744fe1cfd5429543`) reads `{"mode":"100755","path":"rotate-keys.sh","size":244}`. The recursive listing reported `truncated: false`, so that is the complete tree, and `scripts/` contains exactly this one tracked file.

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Mode in git | `100755` (regular file, executable) |
| Blob sha | `f9829bbba1abbf48558fd4cc88931916132a64c7` |
| Size | `244` bytes |

## Git mode vs. working-tree bits

There is no working-tree copy to compare against — nothing on this branch is checked out anywhere I can see, so no divergence between git's mode and on-disk permissions can be observed or claimed. The one local copy I pulled to read the contents landed as `-rw-r--r--`, but that is an artifact of how the broker transfers file bytes (it does not carry the executable bit), **not** a permission recorded in the repository. Only the `100755` above is authoritative.

For what it's worth, the file's own header comment says the bit is load-bearing: it is invoked directly by `.github/workflows/rotate.yml` rather than via `bash`, so it must stay executable — and it currently is.
